concepts.definition: Review at the sprint-close boundary under the authority cited by the manifest. It classifies reviewed items and debt entries, checks durable evidence and changed surfaces, and determines required durable follow-up.

grounding.quote:
Sprint close begins by moving the manifest to `status: closing`. While
closing: new iteration inside that sprint is frozen; every included ticket
or iteration entry is reviewed against the manifest; accumulated evidence
is checked for durability; changed surfaces are walked against cited
authority; deferred compliance is classified; paydown tickets are opened
where debt must survive past the close review (P6, P4b; rc.2
#sprint-close-review).

concepts.label: Sprint close review

concepts.definition: Item outcomes are accepted, local_paydown, design_reframe, requirement_reprice, product_reprice and remove. For the predicate that the item is accepted as compliant under sprint authority, accepted maps to accept/satisfied; local_paydown to local_repair/falsified; the three repricing outcomes to re_enter/invalid_basis; remove to falsified with no matching disposition. Debt-entry outcomes accepted, ticketed, repriced and removed have the corresponding mappings. A repricing layer is a declared change-class fact accompanying the core value as domain outcome.

grounding.quote: | `remove` | none | falsified | the work is backed out or kept out of closure; the reason for removal is the counterexample. No disposition of ACTIVATION §3 has this condition, because removal does not require a violated governing relation or a competing truth path |

The mappings
add no disposition and no core value. The condition for `closed`
above requires an outcome for every item and debt entry, not a
`satisfied` one. The mappings are new in this corpus.

concepts.label: Close classifications and debt outcomes

concepts.definition: A durable unit of work with one authoritative record. Its default carrier is one Markdown file; contract, history, state transitions, stable identity, searchability and closure semantics belong to the record irrespective of carrier.

grounding.quote:
Each ticket has one durable authoritative record; the default carrier is
one markdown file. A repository or external tracker carrier is lawful only
when it preserves the required ticket contract, history, state transition,
stable identity, searchability and closure semantics without a co-equal
local copy

concepts.label: Ticket authoritative record

concepts.definition: One admitted upstream work item with more than one build-tenant execution line. Upstream authority and tenant-local tickets have distinct identities and lifecycles. This member owns the work-item/ticket-lifecycle relation in urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy; PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8 owns tenant identity and realisation meaning.

grounding.quote:
A multi-build-tenant work item is one admitted upstream work item with more
than one build-tenant execution line. The upstream authority and each
tenant-local ticket retain distinct identities and lifecycles.

concepts.label: Multi-build-tenant work item

concepts.definition: Type identifies the kind of work record. The minimum common population is feature, bug, spike and chore; projects may add types, and the default set is expected to suffice for most cases.

grounding.quote:
The minimum common set of ticket types is `feature`, `bug`, `spike` and
`chore`. A project may add more; the default set should be enough for
most cases
(P3; rc.2 #allowed-types).

concepts.label: Ticket type

concepts.definition: Category specifies execution or migration discipline. Its minimum common population is ordinary and implementation_migration. Implementation migration is governed replacement of an implementation truth path across producers, consumers, projections and proof surfaces; examples include replacing a tracker/read-model family, migrating every producer and consumer to a public interface before closure, and removing an authoritative bridge or compatibility facade.

grounding.quote:
`implementation_migration` is
used when the ticket is not "change code until tests pass" but a governed
replacement of one implementation truth path with another across producers,
consumers, projections and proof surfaces:

concepts.label: Ticket category

concepts.definition: The intake-triage declaration of where a change lawfully re-enters the constitutional chain, using SPEC_METHOD §4 classes. Common, nonexclusive pairings are feature with goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice or design_reframe; bug with requirement_reprice, design_reframe or realization_refactor; chore with design_reframe or realization_refactor. A spike remains exploratory while carrying its current triage class.

grounding.quote:
Ticket type and change class are orthogonal: type answers what kind of
work record this is; change class answers where the change lawfully
re-enters the constitutional chain. A ticket records the `change_class`
declared by intake triage, using the classes of
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes) (P4b, P2; rc.2
#change-class).

concepts.label: Ticket change class

concepts.definition: A source-described triage operation consuming computed classification for owner/layer traversal, complete relevant public membership and value delta, accepted-design scope, trace coverage and rule-determined treatment. For bugs it walks upward from the realised surface and associates the highest missing or insufficient governing layer with its lawful re-entry class.

grounding.quote:
Triage consumes the computed classification of
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#computed-classification-and-treatment) for
the declared owner and layer traversal, the complete relevant public
membership and value delta, the accepted-design scope and trace coverage,
and the rule-determined treatment. The owning work carrier references that
exact result and its residuals; a new role does not repeat an unchanged
walk (P4b, P2; rc.2 #upward-propagation-check).

concepts.label: Upward propagation check

concepts.definition: The minimum ticket status population is backlog, active and completed. Ticket/local statuses, lanes, sprint statuses, migration_strategy, library_usage and recorded change_class are declared carrier states, not evaluation results. Backlog is accepted durable work outside current focus; active is the bounded execution set; completed is closed historical work.

grounding.quote:
The ticket statuses, any local state a project adds, the lanes below, the
sprint statuses of §3 and the `migration_strategy` and `library_usage`
values of §6 are declared states of their carriers, not results, and map
to no core value; the recorded `change_class` is a declared state under
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes).

`backlog`
is accepted durable work that should remain visible but is not part of the
current execution focus; `active` is the current bounded execution set;
`completed` is closed work retained as history.

concepts.label: Declared work-carrier states and lanes

concepts.definition: One run-scoped contract for every execution governed by the described method. The smallest lawful source carrier is selected by required lifetime after establishing upstream work authority: an exact admitted ticket, durable ticket, admitted sprint with manifest-local iteration, or intake-drafted run contract. Ticket-shaped means required categorisation, closure criteria, proof, non-closure conditions and fields, without creating ticket identity or lane state.

grounding.quote:
Every execution governed by this method uses one run-scoped execution
contract. The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the
smallest lawful source carrier: first establish the applicable upstream
work authority, then select the first matching row below. For work inside
an admitted sprint the local carrier boundary is that sprint; otherwise it
is the current run (P2, P4b, P6; rc.2 #work-carrier-to-execution-rule).

concepts.label: Run-scoped execution contract

concepts.definition: F13 explains work-carrier rules through stated commitments and instance premises: lifetimes, several apparent work-state surfaces, several tenants, migrations and variable carrier forms. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are independent where cited; P4b derives from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts; P5 derives from P0/P6 with the open-world premise. The table distinguishes consequences, member policy, external ownership and consumers; §10 records dispositions and decides nothing.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises, which the commitments do
not supply, are named in the rows as follows: lifetimes, work and its
obligations last one run, one bounded batch or longer; several surfaces,
goals, tickets, comments, boards and summaries can each appear to state
the same work state; several tenants, one work item may be realised in
more than one build tenant; migrations, some work replaces one
authoritative truth path with another across producers, consumers and
proofs; carriers vary, a project may keep its carriers in files, trackers
or services.

concepts.label: F13 work-carrier foundation-to-law account

concepts.definition: The table's eleven consumer routes respectively concern: lifetime selection and carrier binding (SPEC_METHOD, PRODUCT_DEFINITION, CONFORMANCE 41, judgment continuity); admitted execution (ACTIVATION, ODD); authority/projections (PRODUCT_DEFINITION, recommended shapes); sprint batching (SPEC_METHOD, UX, CONFORMANCE 48, status, closure and manifest); triage (SPEC_METHOD, sprint admission, carrier selection and ticket shape); tenant lifecycles (SPEC_METHOD §11, PRODUCT_DEFINITION); migration (DESIGN_MODULE, status and migration shape); assessment/rulings (EVALUATION, EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, computed classification, recurrence); closure/tests (SPEC_METHOD consistency/evidence, EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, ASSURANCE, milestones); term binding (internal admission/closure only); carrier shapes/reading (no separate consumer). Consumers apply owning rules without adding decisions.

grounding.quote:
Consumers of these rows, where an actor enters them (FOUNDATIONS §3
Foundation to law, Consumers), one list per row, each consumer linked to
its own locus:

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

concepts.label: Work-carrier consumer routes

concepts.definition: Admission validates a contract against its cited product outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis without admitting that basis. Contract states include drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded. Basis admission or renewal belongs to the selected goals-wave owner or explicitly bounded proxy and remains durably legible in existing goals or ticket authority.

grounding.quote:
Admission validates a contract against its cited product outcome,
prerequisite or experiment basis and does not admit that basis (ACTIVATION
§1). Admission or renewal of the basis belongs to the authority owning the
selected goals work wave, or its explicitly bounded proxy, and stays
durably legible in the existing goals or ticket authority

concepts.label: Contract admission distinct from basis admission

concepts.definition: Evaluation criteria identify progress/completion, while non-closure conditions identify continuing failure despite local green proof; together they are the work's local gain function.

grounding.quote:
An execution contract should expose both what counts as progress or
completion and what still counts as failure even when some local proof is
green. At minimum it should make `evaluation_criteria` and
`non_closure_conditions` visible. These are the local gain function for
the work

concepts.label: Evaluation and non-closure conditions

concepts.definition: Ticket and work-instruction terms are resolved under PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 using the cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis, affected scope and any authorised semantic relation.

grounding.quote:
Ticket and work-instruction terms resolve under the bounded-context
semantic resolution of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5. A ticket may use an
unqualified term when its cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis
and affected scope select exactly one bounded-context meaning

concepts.label: Bounded-context term binding

conditions: ticket_category is implementation_migration
concepts.definition: A ticket-local authority surface containing an explicit migration declaration and live Markdown checklist. The declaration names strategy, exact affected scope, every excluded/disjoint product or compatibility scope and deterministic routing, old/new truth paths or contracts, both old/new producer and consumer sets, every derived projection/report/status/proof surface, and migration closure law.

grounding.quote:
The declaration states: the migration strategy used for this work item; the
exact affected migration scope; every explicitly excluded or disjoint
product or compatibility scope with its deterministic routing relation; the
old truth path or superseded contract; the new truth path or authoritative
contract; the producer set for the old and the new path; the consumer set
for the old and the new path; every projection, report, status surface and
proof surface derived from that contract family; and the closure law for
the migration.

concepts.label: Implementation migration ticket

concepts.definition: Upstream migration tickets publish or admit the new authoritative source carrier. Downstream tickets harden prompt assembly, projections, reports, dossiers, review surfaces and other consumers. Their authored dependency chain runs source carrier to downstream consumers.

grounding.quote:
When one migration
wave introduces a new source carrier and then its prompt, projection or
read-model consumers, the dependency chain runs `source carrier ->
downstream consumers`, never the reverse.

concepts.label: Migration source-carrier ticket

concepts.definition: Migration work on consumers downstream of the source-carrier ticket, including prompt, projection, read-model and review surfaces.

grounding.quote:
Tickets that harden prompt assembly, projections, reports, dossiers, review
surfaces or other downstream consumers depend on those upstream source
tickets.

concepts.label: Downstream migration ticket

concepts.definition: Migration strategy values are inside_out_hard_break and fundamental_re_adoption. Library-use values are none, consume and extend, distinguishing local rebuilding, consumption and extension of a reusable library/commonisation surface before local implementation lands.

grounding.quote:
The required fields are `migration_strategy`, with the values
`inside_out_hard_break` and `fundamental_re_adoption`, and
`library_usage`, with the values `none`, `consume` and `extend`.

An implementation migration ticket declares whether the active boundary is
rebuilding a pattern locally, consuming an existing reusable library or
commonisation surface, or extending that surface before the local
implementation lands; `library_usage` records which

concepts.label: Migration strategy and library-use domains

concepts.definition: A ticket-specific review surface for functional migration questions, a named interface-by-interface closure checklist, ordered breaks and break-to-closure mappings. These are described review operations and document roles, not performed reviews.

grounding.quote:
For a core-interface, carrier or authoritative-contract migration, the
ticket includes an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist` before tests can be
used as closure evidence. The checklist is a named walk of every live
interface that can still bypass, reinterpret, replay or project the
migrating truth path

concepts.label: Migration review and execution documents

concepts.definition: Independent assessment is distinct from authoring, self-review and the decision owner's acceptance. Tier-1 assessment/acceptance laws are cited to EVALUATION §§3,5 and closed-result reuse to ACTIVATION §7; this member specifies their work-carrier consequences.

grounding.quote:
The generic law is tier 1: a constructor's self-review is construction
output and the independent-assessment protocol is
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment); acceptance as the
decision owner's disposition, and closure by stated condition rather than
by reviewer approval, is [EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance); reuse
of a closed result is [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse).
This section states what those laws require of work carriers.

concepts.label: Independent assessment and acceptance distinction

concepts.definition: Reusable records in the owning work carrier: residual judgment J carries its question, exact subject/basis, computed facts/evidence, actor/authority, conclusion/scope, uncertainty and concrete revising observation; owner ruling O carries original wording, owner, subject/basis, permitted scope/effects, conditions and source separately from agent interpretation. C, J and O are source annotations, not newly instantiated judgment populations.

grounding.quote:
A residual judgment that another activation needs is recorded once, with
its owning work, in the existing carrier selected under §5. The record
identifies the question; the exact subject and governing basis; the
supporting computed facts and evidence; the responsible actor and its
authority; the conclusion and its scope; the uncertainty; and a concrete
revising observation that lets a consumer determine whether the conclusion
still applies.

concepts.label: Recorded judgment and owner ruling

concepts.definition: Retained, superseded, deferred and withdrawn are obligation states set by the owning authority after repricing, with evidence links. They accept no candidate and map to no core value; they differ from assessed-candidate acceptance dispositions and predecessor-claim dispositions evaluated by qualification.

grounding.quote:
The four repricing dispositions are recorded states of the obligation,
set by its owning authority; they are not results and map to no core
value.

concepts.label: Obligation repricing states

concepts.definition: A work claim closes by the conjunction of its applicable declared obligations, valid exact-scope evidence, required applicable judgments/rulings and absence of active non-closure conditions. This section owns the condition applied by SPEC_METHOD §4 Consistency gate.

grounding.quote:
This condition is the
[conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results) with the
declared obligations as required coverage. This section owns the
closure condition of a work claim;
[SPEC_METHOD §4 Consistency gate](SPEC_METHOD.md#consistency-gate)
applies it as the gate over a declared change span.

concepts.label: Condition-based work-claim closure

concepts.definition: Tests are proof projections from admitted work authority. The recommended derivation for every substantive test is ticket → intake triage → lawful re-entry → governing requirement/design/module/published function/carrier/closure surface → test expectation.

grounding.quote:
ticket -> intake triage -> lawful re-entry point -> governing requirement,
design, module, published function, carrier, or closure surface -> test expectation

concepts.label: Test authority and expectations

concepts.definition: One work-state authority chain assigns the bounded wave to goals, ticket state to the ticket, subordinate milestone state to milestone authority, and realisation decisions to accepted design. Comments, dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections.

grounding.quote:
Work state has one authority chain: goals own the bounded work wave, the
ticket owns ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone
state (§1), and accepted design owns realisation decisions. Comments,
dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections

concepts.label: Work-state authority and projections

concepts.definition: Three recommended document examples, not instantiated work: the active SPRINT-2026-04-30-operational-projection manifest for operational-projection-ux; ordinary active feature T-001 adding the Product layer, product_reprice/product re-entry, dated 2026-04-07 with high priority; active bug B-010 replacing mixed gap projection, implementation_migration/inside_out_hard_break, library_usage none with boundary-specific rationale, design_reframe/design_surface re-entry dated 2026-04-20. Markdown titles supply descriptive headings, and the examples carry fields, authority/context, scope/acceptance and links or migration declaration/checklist.

grounding.quote:
These shapes are the recommended carriers of the fields and sections the
rules above require; a project may bind another shape that carries the
same fields

An implementation migration ticket, carrying the declaration, fields and
checklist of §6:

concepts.label: Recommended sprint and ticket templates

conditions: The default local-file carrier is used.
concepts.definition: Humans and agents read active files directly; backlog stays durably searchable outside immediate focus; rg suffices for finding active work; neither database nor board is required. The sample commands search headings/status/type/goal in active or backlog folders and ticket IDs across tickets.

grounding.quote:
The default local-file carrier assumes that humans and agents can read the
active ticket folder directly; that backlog remains searchable durable work
without competing with the active lane for immediate attention; that `rg`
is sufficient for finding active work; and that no database or board is
required

concepts.label: Default local-file operating mode

concepts.definition: Surface roles are separated: goals identify the current broad wave; SPEC_METHOD supplies constitutional change class/re-entry; sprints price a bounded batch's proof/evidence/paydown; tickets identify durable work and state; comments record proposals, arguments, decisions, reviews and handoffs; POSTING_GUIDE specifies comment publication structure/naming. This avoids goals as overloaded backlog, deferred work diluting active focus, comments as informal task status, or boards as accidental authority.

grounding.quote:
The goals surface: what broad work wave
matters now. SPEC_METHOD: what constitutional change class and re-entry
point govern the work. Sprints: what bounded execution batch is currently
pricing proof, evidence and paydown. Tickets: what durable units of work
exist and what state they are in. Comments: what was proposed, argued,
decided, reviewed or handed off. POSTING_GUIDE: how comment-layer
publications are structured and named.

concepts.label: Relationships among work surfaces

concepts.definition: A provenance ledger claiming conservation of rc.2 TICKET_METHOD rows at named current loci. Heading-only core-model, sprint-rules and ticket-rules rows are marked inapplicable; substantive rows are routed to §§1–9 or named external owners. Routes are provenance only. Recorded generalisations replace profile-specific graph/AssetSurface/UX/F_D/F_P and appointment/design-method terminology with published-function/carrier/user-interface/deterministic/constructive-or-probabilistic/coordinating/design-profile terms; tenant carrier context moves to PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8; §6/§8 code blocks are claimed verbatim, including American spellings and Product.

grounding.quote:
Rows of rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md received by this member. Anchors are into
rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of this file unless another
member is named. Every conserved row is restated in this member's own
text; a route is provenance only.

concepts.label: Ticket-method source disposition ledger

conditions: Adopted by a Product under an exact calculus basis.
concepts.definition: Tier-3 optional, application-neutral model-family signature for immutable application histories over externally changing subjects. Stable concept identity is urn:stdo:concept:traversal-occurrence-profile, owned in urn:stdo:bounded-context:traversal-occurrence-profile. It imports a_c by reference without amendment or universal execution theory; adoption does not import consumer identities.

grounding.quote:
Tier 3. The `a_c` traversal occurrence profile over mutable subjects: an
optional model-family signature for immutable application histories.

Adoption is optional. The profile imports one exact `a_c` basis and
instantiates one closed model-family signature under that basis's record
and model laws. It does not amend `a_c`, does not become part of every

Instance premises are I1 externally changing reality with a stable subject binding, I2 one exact selected a_c basis, and I3 separately identified effects under owner-issued grants. P0 is recovered, P1/P3/P6 independent, P4b derived from P0/P2 and P5 from P0/P6. Closed vocabularies, occurrence identity inputs and identity/causal acyclicity are profile policy; subject interpretation, adoption, authority, precedence, event/frontier laws, causal admissions, compatible territory containment and separately authorised snapshot/rollback are Product choices.

concepts.label: Closed occurrence semantic-object sorts

conditions: A sprint enters close review.
exceptions: Local paydown debt may survive only where its governing method permits explicit follow-up.

grounding.quote:
A sprint may move to
`closed` only when every item and every debt entry is classified and the
resulting paydown or repricing work is durable. Sprint close can accept
local paydown debt only when the governing method allows that debt to
survive as explicit follow-up; it cannot accept hidden authority drift

constraints.statement: Set the manifest to closing, freeze new iteration, review every included ticket/iteration against it, check evidence durability, walk changed surfaces against cited authority, classify deferred compliance, and open paydown tickets for surviving debt. Classify every reviewed item into exactly one of the six outcomes and every debt entry before closed; resulting paydown/repricing work must be durable. Hidden authority drift cannot be accepted.

conditions: A close classification or debt-entry outcome is recorded or combined with other results.

grounding.quote:
the classification consumes
the core results of the item's review and stays separate from them, as
acceptance stays separate from assessment

constraints.statement: Each classification consumes but remains separate from assessment and takes exactly one core value for its stated acceptance predicate at the cited sprint boundary. Accepted means compliant; local_paydown is falsified by ticketed local debt while the governing relation remains coherent; authority changes instead require repricing/invalid_basis. Design repricing changes accepted design, requirement repricing changes a governing requirement, and product repricing changes product definition. Removal is falsified by its removal reason without requiring a violated relation or competing truth path and has no matching disposition. Repricing layer names are domain facts, not additional results. Debt outcomes map on the analogous debt-acceptance predicate. These mappings add neither dispositions nor core values; closed requires outcomes for all entries, not satisfied outcomes. Remaining debt, needed repricing and removal must never be read as compliance.

grounding.quote:
For a local
file, the filename should carry a stable id and a short slug. Recommended
local-file naming:

constraints.statement: Each ticket has exactly one durable authoritative record. A repository/tracker replacement must preserve the ticket contract, history, state transitions, stable identity, searchability and closure semantics without a co-equal local copy. For local files, a stable ID plus short slug is recommended, exemplified by T-001-add-product-layer.md, B-002-fix-reset-manifest-id.md, S-003-evaluate-integration-capability.md and C-004-clean-up-trace-tags.md.

conditions: Backlog or active work has multiple genuine tenant execution lines.
exceptions: Completed tickets are outside retroactive application unless reopened or explicitly repriced.
Upstream-only work requires no tenant duplicate yet; single-tenant work requires no sibling duplicate.
constraints.statement: Retain one upstream source/product/design authority ticket and one suffixed tenant-local ticket per execution line, with a tenant mnemonic in both ID and filename. One ticket cannot close multiple tenant lifecycles; status, proof, closure, blockers, repricing and reopening stay tenant-local, with no masking by another tenant's green status. A tenant duplicate should record source_ticket and build_tenant; the latter identifies the product how.build_tenants entry. A path, alias or tracker label substitutes for identity only if product definition binds it. The unsuffixed base may remain upstream authority. Duplication is only for genuinely multiple tenant lines, not all tickets; B-030 with B-030-T1 and B-030-T2 is a recommended illustration.

grounding.quote:
Each ticket records at least `id`, `title`, `type`, `ticket_category`,
`status`, `goal`, `change_intent`, `change_class`, `re_entry_point`,
`triaged_at`, `created_at` and `updated_at`

constraints.statement: Every ticket records at least id, title, type, ticket_category, status, goal, change_intent, change_class, re_entry_point, triaged_at, created_at and updated_at. Recommended extras are priority, dependencies, links, intake_source, affected_boundary, source_ticket for duplication/derivation, and build_tenant for tenant-local work. An implementation_migration ticket additionally requires migration_strategy and library_usage, governing_library for consume/extend, and library_rationale for none. A tenant-local implementation migration requires build_tenant and, when derived/duplicated from an upstream source/product/design ticket, source_ticket. For execution-contract admission, a runtime-drafted contract should additionally carry at minimum target_truth, superseded_truth when relevant, closure_law, evaluation_criteria, non_closure_conditions and proof_surface.

grounding.quote:
`spike` as exploratory
work that still carries the current triage class and should terminate
either in a more specific downstream ticket or in an explicit decision
that no further substantive change is required.

constraints.statement: Record intake triage's declared change_class using SPEC_METHOD §4. The listed type/class pairings are common examples, not exhaustive restrictions. A spike carries the current triage class and should end in a more specific downstream ticket or explicit no-further-substantive-change decision. Type, category and change class remain independent dimensions; bug/implementation_migration/design_reframe is expressly consistent.

conditions: Triage classifies work; the detailed upward stop rules apply to bugs.

grounding.quote:
Before declaring `realization_refactor` for a bug, establish that the
current requirement and the accepted realising design govern the affected
behaviour and remain sufficient for the authorised outcome. Their presence
proves no coverage. Missing or ambiguous evidence leaves the affected
treatment unknown; it is not proof that the governing layer itself is
absent (P6).

constraints.statement: Reference the exact computed classification and residuals; a new role does not repeat an unchanged walk. Before realization_refactor, establish that current requirement and accepted design govern the affected behaviour and suffice for the authorised outcome; presence proves no coverage and missing/ambiguous evidence leaves treatment unknown rather than proving a missing layer. A public violation selects no new contract; re-enter a governing owner only for explicitly changed desired outcome or established insufficiency. Check each layer, stopping at the highest missing/insufficient layer: missing/insufficient requirement→requirement_reprice and its owner; sufficient requirement with missing/insufficient design→design_reframe/Design; actual Goal/Intent/Product change→its matching repricing class/owner; sufficient requirement/design with implementation deviation→realization_refactor, repair or reject candidate. Unresolved meaning remains J; reserved choice remains O.
constraints.uncertainty: The source-disposition ledger describes a first-missing-layer walk; this tension is separately retained.

conditions: The ticket carries substantive work.

grounding.quote:
the declared `change_intent`, the lawful `change_class`, the lawful
`re_entry_point`, and when triage occurred in `triaged_at`

constraints.statement: The durable ticket records change_intent, lawful change_class, lawful re_entry_point and triaged_at exactly as declared by intake triage.

grounding.quote:
a declared state is never combined as an evaluation result, so
a ticket marked `completed`, or a sprint marked `closed`, cannot stand in
for a `satisfied` result

constraints.statement: Ticket/sprint statuses, local states, lanes, migration/library values and recorded change class map to no core value. An evaluation reading a state returns its own predicate-bound core value. Close classifications/debt outcomes are separately mapped results; completed/closed status cannot substitute for satisfied.

grounding.quote:
Backlog tickets live at the product definition's
`ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog` binding, by default
`.ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/`; active tickets at
`ticketing.tickets.lanes.active`, by default `.ai-workspace/tickets/active/`;
completed tickets move to `ticketing.tickets.lanes.completed`, by default
`.ai-workspace/tickets/completed/`

constraints.statement: Locate backlog, active and completed tickets through product bindings ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog, .active and .completed, defaulting respectively to .ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/, active/ and completed/. Completed tickets move to the completed binding. Lanes keep active execution small and searchable without displacing deferred work into goals/comments.

conditions: A derived surface or projected frame leaves a named lifecycle or proof question unresolved.

grounding.quote:
If a derived surface or projected frame of this member is insufficient,
the actor reads this member only for the named unresolved lifecycle or
proof question and cites the clauses used

constraints.statement: The source prescribes reading this member only for the named unresolved lifecycle/proof question and citing the clauses used; prompt construction is assigned to ACTIVATION §2. This is interpreted as a represented reading policy, not executed here.
constraints.uncertainty: The source attributes this rule to an rc.2 compression while explicitly saying no rc.2 body states it.

grounding.quote:
The standing of these consequences is stated in
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law).
The table accounts for §1 to §9, and for POSTING_GUIDE §2, §7 and §9,
which have no family table of their own. §10 records dispositions and
decides nothing.

constraints.statement: The table adds no decisions beyond its cited rules. It requires recording obligations before run return on sufficiently lasting carriers, one exact authority chain, and explicit rebinding without rivals. Comments remain provisional posts until adopted by the owning surface and retain their own discussion state; milestone acceptance establishes only its own claim. Sprint batching defers only declared local proof as escrow, never triage; law-changing work leaves the sprint for its own layer. Member choices include carrier kinds/selection, minimum fields/types/categories/statuses, defaults/lanes/shapes, sprint mechanics/classifications, migration declarations/checklists/thresholds/order and repricing states/reconciliation order. Product definition owns carrier locations, rebinding, admission mechanism and durable result/evidence surfaces; governing method owns surviving sprint debt; SPEC_METHOD owns change classes/migration law; POSTING_GUIDE owns comment structure/states; EVALUATION/ACTIVATION own assessment/reuse; FOUNDATIONS owns conjunction/table standing; ASSURANCE owns general test law. Consumers inherit these bounds, including no admission/compliance/closure from a sprint status/classification, no duplicate UX mapping, and no self-review relabelled by fresh context.
constraints.uncertainty: External owners and omitted local sections are cited rather than reconstructed.

conditions: Select the first matching case after establishing applicable upstream authority.

grounding.quote: | no applicable upstream work authority exists | no execution contract is admitted | do not create a ticket as substitute authority; stop or re-enter |

constraints.statement: Use one run-scoped contract. Ordered cases: no upstream authority→no admitted contract, no substitute-authority ticket, stop/re-enter; exact admitted ticket covers work→derive/reuse it without duplicate; authority exists, no exact ticket and independent state survives the local boundary→durable ticket plus contract, created/updated only under ticket-state authority; authority exists, no exact ticket and work stays in an admitted sprint without post-close state→manifest plus one local iteration, no durable ticket; authority exists, no exact ticket/sprint and work ends in this run without surviving state→intake-drafted run contract, no durable ticket. The local boundary is admitted sprint, otherwise current run. Ticket absence neither requires nor authorises creation. An exact product-authorised instruction may provide one-run authority; generic request or model-widened scope cannot. An explicit ticket-state-authority instruction selects durability but neither admits a contract nor widens upstream authority.

grounding.quote:
A carrier's lane, status or
prose that asserts admission without those coordinates is not admission
evidence, and the contract it describes remains drafted or rejected.

constraints.statement: ACTIVATION §1 owns drafting/admission, execution-start conditions, coordinates and recording every result, withheld closure and residual obligation before return, including refusal without a durable result/evidence surface. Use product-bound mechanism/surface; if ticket or manifest is that surface, record admitted result and coordinates there. Presence, lane, active status or admission prose without coordinates is not admission evidence; the contract remains drafted/rejected. Absent/rejected admission returns missing authority without execution. Before return, retain a surviving obligation as sprint-local if its lifetime stays within an admitted sprint; otherwise as durable ticket only with ticket-state authority; absent that authority use the named durable result/evidence surface or authorised enclosing carrier, mark closure withheld on ticket-state authority and return re-entry. Execution and closure use the same admitted categorisation, criteria, proof surface and non-closure conditions, with state continuing through proof, gap analysis and repricing.
constraints.uncertainty: The full admission coordinate schema and step semantics reside in unsupplied ACTIVATION §1.

grounding.quote:
The runtime execution flow should treat a ticket, a sprint entry or a
drafted work contract as an admission candidate, never as automatic truth;

constraints.statement: Runtime flow should treat tickets, sprint entries and drafted contracts as admission candidates, never automatic truth; contracts carry at least drafted/admitted/rejected/superseded states. An admitted contract should be logged in runtime/event truth and available to prompt assembly and later closure checking. Self-certification is refused under ACTIVATION §1. Contract admission validates but never admits its cited outcome/prerequisite/experiment basis; active status, lane or an admitted/retained contract never admits a growth basis. Basis admission/renewal belongs to the goals-wave owner or bounded proxy and must remain durably legible.

exceptions: Debt outside the claimed acceptance path is not by itself a non-closure condition; deferral still requires SPEC_METHOD §7 path-relative authority and explicit disposition.

grounding.quote:
Residual implementation debt outside the claimed acceptance path is not by
itself a non-closure condition. It may be deferred only under the
path-relative authority and explicit disposition rules of
[SPEC_METHOD §7](SPEC_METHOD.md#constitutional-migration-options) (P2).

constraints.statement: A contract should expose progress/completion and continuing failure, at minimum evaluation_criteria and non_closure_conditions. Typical migration non-closure conditions are a still-passing old authoritative path in affected scope, accepted mixed old/new proof, proxy/partial interface in acceptance, reachable competing/ambiguous executable authority on the claimed acceptance path, or unreconciled ticket/product/proof wording. These conditions are not optional commentary.

grounding.quote:
An unresolved or multiply resolved material term blocks execution-contract
admission and closure for the affected claim. Opening or updating the
ticket records the pressure and does not cure it; resolution re-enters at
the authority that owns the missing context or semantic relation

constraints.statement: Use an unqualified term only where cited product, re-entry, execution basis and scope select exactly one bounded-context meaning. Across contexts or competing material meanings, cite product-definition disambiguation or an owner-authorised import/translation/equivalence/disambiguation carrier; reference rather than duplication is permitted. Prose, actor familiarity, matching glossary headings, tenant placement and comment context cannot choose meaning or transfer authority. An unresolved or multiply resolved material term blocks admission and closure of the affected claim; ticket creation/update does not cure it and resolution re-enters the owning authority.

conditions: ticket_category is implementation_migration
exceptions: If no excluded/disjoint scope exists, explicit absence satisfies that checklist item; silence does not.

grounding.quote:
A ticket with `ticket_category: implementation_migration` carries both an
explicit migration declaration block and a hard migration checklist. Both
are part of the ticket authority, not optional commentary.

constraints.statement: Require the declaration and at least this live Markdown checklist: name exact affected scope; name excluded/disjoint Product/compatibility scopes and deterministic routing or explicit absence; name old/new paths; list new producers/consumers and projection/read-model surfaces; remove/demote old authority in affected scope; reject mixed-state closure evidence; remove/reprice mixed-old/new tests; check recurring patterns against library/commonisation surfaces; declare library use and governing library/rationale; for multi-tenant backlog/active work carry one tenant lifecycle with siblings on suffixed tickets; reconcile ticket/product/proof claims before closure. Require migration_strategy in {inside_out_hard_break, fundamental_re_adoption} and library_usage in {none, consume, extend}. Consume/extend names governing_library; none explains in library_rationale that no reusable surface applies, the pattern remains boundary-specific, or it is not yet a lawful recurrence/commonisation candidate. SPEC_METHOD §7 owns migration law; this is its minimum ticket-local enforcement surface.

exceptions: An explicitly declared and ticket-justified retained compatibility feature may retain an old path.
Deterministically routed non-overlapping product scope outside affected scope retains its own current authority.

grounding.quote:
if a ticket was
marked `completed` and later review shows checked closure items are false
on the current tree, the ticket is reopened or an explicitly linked
successor ticket is created, because a false closure claim is a
ticket-method defect, not only a code defect

constraints.statement: Block closure while an old authoritative interface passes normal execution within declared scope unless retained compatibility is explicit. Old paths cannot silently remain authoritative; compatibility must be named as compatibility, justified in the ticket and never inferred from code. Mixed green tests, proxies and partial implementations do not establish completion. False checked closure on the current tree after completed requires reopening or an explicitly linked successor. An intermediate product slice may be accepted only under SPEC_METHOD §7 path-relative promotion and derived identity/criteria that ticket wording cannot narrow. The migration remains active until checklist/final law are satisfied; active status renews no exhausted slice growth authority. Removal/demotion/closure-proof work may continue only within that law's bound; further material producer/consumer growth needs another SPEC_METHOD §3 admitted basis.
constraints.uncertainty: Slice derivation, path-relative bounds and basis admission details are externally defined.

grounding.quote: Unclassified inherited implementation blocks closure (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: For inside_out_hard_break, carry a full best-guess migrating-interface inventory, deepest-source-outward break sequence, old seam intentionally severed by each break and expected negative proof per break. For fundamental_re_adoption, carry explicit human product-authority selection; comparison with bounded evolution across product value, feedback latency, authority risk, reversibility, total cost and retained predecessor semantics; bounded abort/re-entry condition; sideways reference/prior implementation boundary as source material; module/interface adjudication surface; and a carry_across, redundant or rewrite classification for every inherited module, interface, carrier, projection and proof surface. Unclassified inherited implementation blocks closure.
constraints.uncertainty: SPEC_METHOD §7 defines the three inherited-implementation classifications; those definitions are not supplied.

conditions: Every implementation migration, irrespective of adopted Product profiles.
exceptions: A third local rebuild can proceed with consume, extend, or a linked explicit do-not-commonise design decision in library_rationale.

grounding.quote:
the second
credible recurrence forces an explicit
library or commonisation review; the third local rebuild is not acceptable
by default.

constraints.statement: Declare local rebuild, consume or extend. Second credible recurrence forces library/commonisation review; if review finds the same pattern in two module boundaries or tickets, a third local rebuild blocks implementation absent a stated exception. Prefer boundary-local cleanup, then tenant-local reusable surface, then shared/common propagation only through separate design re-entry. Adoption of DESIGN_MODULE adds its §10 candidate/design-review refinement without a rival threshold. A discovered pattern remains subject to these thresholds and applicable hard stops; outside them it is repricing input, neither blocking the bounded claim nor requiring a follow-up unless the owner admits that follow-up.
constraints.uncertainty: The external profile's commonisation-candidate refinement is not supplied.

conditions: The same work item is processed across several build tenants; review concerns backlog and active tickets.
exceptions: Upstream source/product/design ticket change can require work beyond tenant-local reopening/repricing/succession.

grounding.quote:
each ticket names its `build_tenant`; each tenant ticket has its
own proof surface and closure law; one tenant's green proof does not stand
in for another tenant's closure; and reopening, repricing and successor
work remain tenant-local unless the upstream source, product or design
ticket itself must change

constraints.statement: Review verifies a separate suffixed ticket per tenant, explicit build_tenant on each, each ticket's own proof surface and closure law, no substitution of another tenant's green proof, and tenant-local reopening/repricing/successor work subject to the upstream-change exception.

grounding.quote:
Passing tests do not satisfy this section by themselves. A slice that keeps
the same semantic centre alive behind typed wrappers, adapter-local policy,
old lists beside new algebra, fallback config or rehydrated dict payloads
still fails migration review even when public behaviour remains green

constraints.statement: Make review concrete enough to prevent rename/adapter/wrapper/happy-path proof from claiming source-truth migration. Core-interface/carrier tickets should include ticket-specific Functional Review Criteria enabling answers to nine questions: replacement of control-flow-owned meaning by admitted source truth; removal rather than relocation of semantic centre; typed/closed law rather than open dict/string/config; main step as pure transform rather than procedural law-making orchestration; effects at edges; direct admitted-carrier consumption rather than reconstructed payload/default/text/legacy truth; projections derived rather than independent authority; existing deterministic checks inform state without structurally blocking the contract's lawful constructive/probabilistic path; recurring patterns explicitly consume/extend reuse rather than rebuild. These are recommended review questions, not independently imposed universal architecture. Passing tests alone do not suffice; retaining the semantic centre behind wrappers, adapter policy, old lists, fallback config or rehydrated dicts still fails.

conditions: A core-interface, carrier or authoritative-contract migration.
exceptions: Compatibility shims satisfy an item only if explicitly justified as retained compatibility.

grounding.quote:
Review rules (P6): a checked box asserts truth on the current tree, not
intended direction; if review shows a checked interface item is false, the
ticket is not closure-ready; an intentionally deferred interface either
names its successor ticket or stays unchecked;

constraints.statement: Before tests can serve as closure evidence, include a named walk of every live interface able to bypass, reinterpret, replay or project the path, each with its own closure criterion. Where present, the checklist should enumerate source builders; closure/register/projection builders; deepest kernels/adapters; wrappers and bootstrap/replay/ingest/resume/query entrypoints; prompts/reports/projections/read models; constructors/materialisers; proof lanes and negative fixtures. Examples require admitted projection consumption without raw-helper authority, read models without silently rebuilding absent carriers, and gap builders without independent closure from open payload rows. Checked means true on the current tree; a false checked item prevents closure readiness. Deferred interfaces name a successor or remain unchecked. Hard-break checklists describe seam inventory before test evidence; re-adoption checklists classify inherited modules/interfaces being carried/dropped/rewritten, with no implicit carry-forward.

conditions: An implementation migration touches a core interface.

grounding.quote:
When the migration has several old interfaces, the ticket also includes a
`Break-To-Closure Map` stating which break closes which closure-law clause;

constraints.statement: Include Required Break Order or equivalent: discover full best-guess interface family; publish/admit new source; deliberately sever one old authoritative seam and keep it broken; rebind deepest kernel; remove/demote old producers; rebind old consumers; reprice projections/reports/prompts/delivery/tests. With several old interfaces, map every break to closure-law clauses. Explicit defects include wrappers carrying old authority, new carrier beside authoritative old read model, renamed proxies/partial old interfaces, constructor/replay/ingest/resume/bootstrap/public-wrapper admission bypass, projections/tests passing without new carrier, fallback invention of policy/identity/target/closure truth, and downstream proof passing while source work remains open.

conditions: A migration ticket seeks closure.
exceptions: An explicitly specified retained compatibility path may survive.
A deterministically routed non-overlapping product scope outside affected scope keeps its own authority and does not block merely because its path works.

grounding.quote:
For a migration ticket, positive behaviour proof is not enough. The proof
surface should include at least one negative or structural proof that
the old path can no longer satisfy the closure law

constraints.statement: Positive behaviour proof is insufficient; the proof surface should include at least one negative/structural proof that the old path cannot satisfy closure law. Example proofs reject the severed seam before downstream progress; fail closed when new carrier is removed; reject legacy payload without admitted carrier; select new truth or fail closed on deliberate disagreement; reject same-name but structurally different carriers/functions/routes/policies/projection sources; and avoid dependence on undeclared local fixtures or mutable sibling workspaces. Keep the ticket open if the old path works normally in affected scope or remains reachable on the claimed acceptance path, subject to explicit compatibility. Where an interface checklist exists, negative proof exercises named public consumers material to closure; bypassing one shim is insufficient if live authority bypasses it through other helpers/loaders/rebuilds.

conditions: Independent assessment is required by a claimed product, qualification, release or explicitly risk-bearing boundary, or added by the governing basis.
exceptions: Independent review is not required for every local implementation step.

grounding.quote:
Independent review is required at
product, qualification, release and explicitly risk-bearing boundaries that
claim it, not for every local implementation step

constraints.statement: Authoring authority is not independent verification authority; the reviewer is not the reviewed subject's author and follows EVALUATION §3. Identify exact subject, basis, scope, exclusions, evidence, verdict and unresolved findings; cite current authority and code/proof paths, not historical commentary alone. Self-review is useful authoring evidence but neither relabelling nor human acceptance makes it independent. Promotion/closure can use a claimed independent review only when its exact subject/verdict are durably traceable in an existing ticket/commentary/qualification/release-evidence carrier; occurrence assertions, unbound summaries and unavailable drafts are not verdicts. No separate receipt/carrier/round is required. Verdicts bind exact claims/hard stops; EVALUATION §5 alone supplies blocking triggers.
constraints.uncertainty: External assessment protocol and promotion-trigger details are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
Ticket state, ticket prose or
an admitted execution contract cannot widen that basis or substitute for
the live-surface assessment the relation requires

constraints.statement: Before the next affected acceptance boundary give a direct/lawfully proxied human ruling durable disposition with source wording separate from interpretation; opening a ticket neither satisfies nor widens it. Where the agentic construction relation applies, identify selected execution basis, bounded affected relations, delegated construction/assessment authority and re-entry conditions; accepted design/existing evidence may be referenced. Ticket state/prose/admitted contract neither widen basis nor substitute for live-surface assessment. A reviewable transition may use existing ticket/commentary/commit/qualification/release evidence with no new state, document type, review round or ceremony. This member owns selection/traceability; ACTIVATION §1 and SPEC_METHOD §8 own execution semantics.

grounding.quote:
J is not O, and recording either cannot create admission,
acceptance, effects or continuation beyond the original grant

constraints.statement: Record once any residual judgment needed by another activation in its owning carrier with all stated coordinates; invent no J for rule-settled questions. Later roles/runs recover it and check applicability rather than re-author unchanged judgment. Changed material facts/evidence, declared revising observation or basis invalidate affected results, preserving original and successor relation, retaining only demonstrably independent results and reassessing affected scope. Role/conversation change alone invalidates nothing; reuse cannot promote unknown facts into premises. Independent assessors may consume valid C but acquire sufficient exact evidence and supply their own independent judgment; author's J is insufficient. Record owner rulings in original terms separately from interpretation; reuse while applicable without widening/re-requesting unchanged authority. Return only affected questions on new ambiguity/material decision change. J is not O and neither record creates admission/acceptance/effects/continuation. Use existing lifetime/result surfaces without separate registry, ticket per judgment or ceremony.

conditions: An obligation is affected by repricing.

grounding.quote:
a recorded disposition is never combined as an evaluation
result, so a retained obligation is never read as satisfied, and a
superseded, deferred or withdrawn one never as discharged

constraints.statement: Give every affected obligation retained/superseded/deferred/withdrawn disposition in the same carrier with owner and evidence links; preserve surviving work, explain changed dependencies, and do not duplicate unaffected history in a parallel ledger. Present owner decisions as short consequence deltas while preserving original rulings. A general continue instruction does not accept undisclosed architecture/scope change. Repricing dispositions are not evaluation results: retained never means satisfied, and superseded/deferred/withdrawn never means discharged. Evaluations reading them return their own predicate-bound core value.

exceptions: Where law requires neither independent review nor reserved acceptance, a result may be recorded without review under ACTIVATION §1, using the existing ticket; sprint-close and design-profile laws still apply.

grounding.quote:
A work claim is complete only when every applicable declared obligation is
satisfied by valid evidence for its exact subject, basis and scope; every
required judgment and owner ruling is present and applicable; and no active
non-closure condition remains. A mandatory obligation whose applicability is
unknown, or whose evidence is insufficient, withholds the dependent claim;
evidence presence alone is not satisfaction. The existing owner decides any
reserved acceptance

constraints.statement: Complete only when every applicable declared obligation has valid exact-subject/basis/scope evidence, every required judgment/ruling is present/applicable, and no active non-closure condition remains. Unknown mandatory applicability or insufficient evidence withholds the dependent claim; evidence presence is insufficient, and reserved acceptance belongs to the existing owner. Review evaluates conditions, not itself closing work. Reuse valid applicable evidence/J/O for unchanged obligations. Material counterexample, changed evidence, stated J revising observation or basis change invalidate affected claim and dependent results before reliance. Unrelated observation stays bounded repricing input without automatic reopening or expansion. Closure records exact evaluated scope, satisfied conditions, evidence and residuals.

grounding.quote:
The implementation may show that a test is stale, incomplete or too
narrow; it cannot by itself authorise changing the expected result.

constraints.statement: Every substantive test should follow the admitted authority derivation chain; current implementation never supplies expected-result authority. Acceptance predicates need a supported applicable entry/state and an obligation under governing operating/threat model. Existing tests cannot authorise excluded threats or superseded guards; changed responsibility requires predicate audit and retirement of unsupported expectations under owning basis without inventing replacement guards. Live authority conflict requires re-entry, not test-only waiver. Reconcile mismatch in order: ticket intent/class/re-entry/target/superseded truth/closure law/evaluation/non-closure fields; triage/lawful owner; cited governing authority; test expectation; implementation. Code is evidence, never arbiter. Update/remove pre-repricing tests only after naming governing ticket and superseding authority change. Stale/ambiguous/authority-deficient tickets re-enter triage before treating code or test as correct. A passing test is closure evidence only if its expectation traces to admitted ticket/authority.

grounding.quote:
Recency, visibility or repetition does not turn a projection into truth.
Contradiction between the owning ticket, its required milestones, the
current goals or the cited acceptance evidence blocks closure. Superseded
evidence remains history and cannot be projected as current acceptance

constraints.statement: Recency, visibility and repetition never promote projections into authority. Contradictions among owning ticket, required milestones, current goals or cited acceptance evidence block closure. Superseded evidence stays history and cannot represent current acceptance.

conditions: Reading or adapting the supplied examples as document templates.

grounding.quote:
- non_closure_conditions: product truth or data contract drift remains hidden
- paydown_policy: open paydown tickets for accepted local debt; reprice authority drift
- closure_law: migration closes only when the old projection is no longer authoritative within the affected scope and mixed old/new proof does not count as acceptance

constraints.statement: The sprint example cites GOALS/PRODUCT/design authority, scopes layout/readability/interaction/visual evidence, excludes product truth/data contract/runtime/governance/new constructive carrier changes, expects realization_refactor, and records UXI-001 relation-line readability with screenshot and pending contrast debt. Its close triggers are timebox, changed-surface volume or design-lead request; closure walks each changed state against authority with screenshots/notes, deferred screenshots/accessibility/replay review, hidden-drift non-closure and paydown-versus-repricing policy. T-001 addresses omitted Product definition and requires PRODUCT in the chain, intent→product→requirements bootstrap and aligned examples/reconstruction. B-010 scopes declared operator-query gap projection, explicitly excludes no scopes, replaces synthetic-convergence fallback with declared-obligation projection plus separately classified fallback gaps, names old/new producer/consumer and query/summary/proof surfaces, and requires old projection de-authorisation plus rejection of mixed proof. Its checklist illustrates the required migration checklist, with all boxes unasserted. Example metadata, paths and placeholders describe templates, not actual work admission, evidence, execution or completion.

grounding.quote:
New law with no predecessor row: the family table at §5, which decides
nothing beyond the rules it cites; the statement in §4 Status that the
ticket and sprint statuses, the lanes and the migration declaration
values are declared states, not results; and the statement in §7
Recorded judgment and owner-ruling continuity that the four repricing
dispositions of an obligation are recorded states, not results.

constraints.statement: Treat routes and conservation assertions as provenance claims, not additional operative rules or verified equivalence. The ledger identifies new family-table law, declared-state/result distinctions and obligation-state/result distinctions; the close mappings are also identified as new at their row. The family table decides nothing beyond cited rules; FOUNDATIONS §3 owns its format and consequence standing.
constraints.uncertainty: Predecessor documents and many routed sections are not supplied, so conservation and verbatim claims cannot be checked.

grounding.quote:
Here occurrence, lineage, frontier, cut and projection name only this
profile's sorts and relations: `Occurrence`, its `lineage_refs` and typed
lineage relations, `EventFrontier`, `SemanticAdmissionCut` and
`Projection`. They claim neither the core's release cut nor its product
lineage, nor any other member's frontier; a `frontier_projection`
judgment judges a `Projection` record and is not an
[AC-011](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-011-projection) projection.

constraints.statement: Occurrence/lineage/frontier/cut/projection refer only to the profile's sorts and relations, not core release cuts/product lineage or other member frontiers. frontier_projection is a judgment about a Projection record, not AC-011 projection. The profile imports signature/RecordKind/Population (§2), records (§3), AC-003 reference closure, traversals/F_D/F_P/F_H (§5), AC-016 composition, basis (§8), FOUNDATIONS results and ACTIVATION effects without restatement. rc.2 anchors route to TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE_PROFILE.md as provenance only.

grounding.quote:
Availability is not adoption. A Product that adopts the profile owns its
subject interpretation, concrete vocabulary, authorities, requirements,
design, implementation and evidence; this member imports none of those
consumer identities

constraints.statement: Availability or inclusion in a method cut does not constitute adoption or authority. Adoption is optional and selects one exact a_c basis/closed signature without amending a_c, applying to every model or supplying universal execution theory. The adopting Product owns subject interpretation, concrete vocabulary, authorities, requirements, design, implementation and evidence; those consumer identities are not imported.

conditions: The Product adopts the occurrence profile and its instance premises.

grounding.quote: By P3 an identity binds its exact inputs, so a traversal applied again to any changed input is a different occurrence; by P4b an established fact is not erased.

constraints.statement: Each exact application is immutable; changed inputs/reapplication mint a new occurrence and corrections append without erasure. Observations/events/projections describe external reality without replacing it; external subject remains reality's carrier. Candidate, judgment, admitting event and materialised relation are distinct; precedence orders admitted facts without deciding authority. Cause is admitted typed lineage, never inferred from time/order/adjacency/containment/correlation. Identity dependency and occurrence/event causal subgraphs are acyclic, ensuring a first cause; this does not assert all lineage graphs acyclic. Projection binds one complete immutable frontier and is not read beyond it; new event means new frontier. All members of one admitted semantic cut share an identical source frontier, successor equals that frontier plus exactly the admitted event, and missing/inconsistent members refuse.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed identity inputs, event scope/frontier laws and full relation definitions lie in unsupplied referenced clauses.

exceptions: A compatible Product signature may declare territory containment instead of exact equality.

grounding.quote: an effect whose outcome the evidence cannot decide stays indeterminate, an established non-attainment of its intended outcome is falsified whether or not its end is established, and no refusal maps to success

constraints.statement: No effect operation is lawful without its matching owner grant; functor kind, traversal, operation, executor, actor, grant and invocation stay separate. invokes_effect requires an exact grant and authorized_by checks operation kind, target and territory; unauthorized/stale effect readiness never dispatches.
